newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar breaks support on mixed sales.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar breaks support on mixed sales.

text.p: London's spot December white sugar contract tumbled through major chart support at $310 as the mixed selling seen earlier in the session gathered pace with the decline in fortunes of the March raws, traders said on Thursday.
Most of the selling was outright in a reaction to a bearish technical picture as trade players joined commission houses in baling out of the nearby contract.
"It's pretty outright stuff, Dec/March is remaining stable between $3.50 and $4.00," said one trader.
"It's having a little technical push on the downside -- it's weak everywhere," he added.
At 1651 GMT December stood $3.20 lower at $309.70, just up from its $309.00 intraday low. March was $3.20 lower at $305.90 and all positions lost ground in wider ranges than of late.
Volume amounted to a solid 2,355 lots and was concentrated in the three front positions.
Technical analysts said December's slight nudge above resistance at $315 during Wednesday's session was just the final failure of the market to move higher.
December has now fallen through the bottom of a downtrend channel dating from a reaction low on September 17.
"We're in a bear run and it doesn't look as if we're going to break out of it for the time being," the trader said. "Consolidation is needed, it's about the only hope we can have."
Physical news included a report that Tunisia bought 13,000 tonnes of white sugar for shipment in June 1997 at a snap tender. Traders said the price paid was $346.50 per tonne c&f.
Activity in Paris closely reflected the fall in London. December slid $3.00 to touch a session low of $309.00 and March was $3.70 down at $305.80. Matif volume totalled 1,434 lots.
